text: Agile is a popular way of working on projects, especially in software development. Instead of doing everything at once, teams use iterative development. They break the project into small parts and work in short phases called sprints, which usually last two to four weeks. At the start of each sprint, the team picks tasks from a prioritized list called the backlog. These tasks are often written as user stories, which describe a feature from the customer's perspective. Every day, the team holds a quick standup meeting to share progress and problems. This flexible approach helps teams adapt quickly to changes and deliver value regularly.
